text: Restaurants theme should not be screened only by branded restaurant traffic; higher-quality Serenity lanes include franchisee unit economics, procurement scale, digital demand capture, foodservice inputs, approved-vendor relationships, and equipment/service infrastructure.

Restaurant POS, loyalty, ordering, payments, and back-office software are high-priority underfollowed nodes because they can control customer data, throughput, labor efficiency, and franchise-system standardization.

Private-label coffee, beverage extracts, DSD beverage service, and foodservice consumables remain promising underfollowed nodes; WEST and FARM are seed names but require filings-based verification of current restaurant customer exposure and financial durability.

Domino's and Yum should be retained primarily as reference leaders for procurement scale, franchisee economics, supply-chain coordination, and digital ordering economics rather than as the only investable expression of the restaurants theme.

Layer 1 universe still needs expansion into foodservice distributors, packaging suppliers, cold-chain logistics, sanitation/maintenance vendors, dairy/cheese/protein suppliers, and restaurant facilities-service companies.

Restaurants should be mapped as a system of traffic demand, franchisee unit economics, procurement, distribution, inputs, equipment, digital rails, labor productivity, and compliance rather than as only consumer-facing brands.

Foodservice procurement access and supplier concentration appear to be high-scoring chokepoints, especially for independent restaurants and smaller franchise systems with low margins and limited bargaining power.

Broadline distributors, cash-and-carry channels, regional distributors, DSD routes, and group purchasing networks should be tracked as hidden bottleneck layers because they affect input cost, switching costs, and replenishment reliability.

Restaurant POS, loyalty, ordering, payments, and back-office software may be an underfollowed infrastructure layer because scaled brands require standardized digital systems across franchise locations.
Commercial kitchen equipment, equipment service, and smart-kitchen workflows can become bottlenecks when brands pursue throughput, labor productivity, smaller footprints, and standardized remodels.

Coffee, tea, extracts, proprietary beverages, and beverage-service infrastructure deserve a separate node because beverage-heavy dayparts and loyalty programs may carry higher-margin growth than generic food traffic.
Foodservice distribution consolidation could raise the strategic value of procurement diversification, regional distributors, and cooperative purchasing alternatives.
Commodity volatility in wings, coffee, dairy, cheese, grains, packaging, and freight can create catalysts for contracted pricing, scale procurement, and approved-supplier consolidation.
High digital and off-premise mix at QSR and specialty beverage concepts supports continued investment in first-party ordering, loyalty, analytics, payments, and delivery-channel optimization.

Need filings-backed verification of actual restaurant-channel revenue mix, approved-vendor status, contract duration, customer concentration, and foodservice exposure for PAR, WEST, FARM, MIDD, THS, and other lower-attention suppliers.

Need to expand public-market mapping beyond the cached universe into broadline distributors, specialty ingredients, frozen bakery/dough, protein processors, dairy/cheese suppliers, packaging, sanitation, cold-chain logistics, facilities services, and restaurant compliance tools.
Need to separate true restaurant-demand beneficiaries from broad consumer staples, industrial, or software companies with only incidental restaurant exposure.

PAR should remain a high-priority underfollowed restaurant-infrastructure candidate because its POS, loyalty, ordering, payments, and back-office stack maps directly to franchise standardization and first-party demand capture, but survival to later layers requires filings-backed proof of enterprise restaurant penetration, retention, and module attach.

WEST should remain in the underfollowed lane as a B2B beverage-input and private-label supplier tied to restaurant foodservice demand, but the key gating issue is whether restaurant and foodservice customers are material enough to overcome debt, capex, and margin risks.

DPZ and YUM should be treated primarily as reference leaders, not underfollowed alpha candidates, because they define franchise procurement, loyalty, unit-economics, and supply-chain models useful for evaluating smaller suppliers.

MIDD is a plausible underfollowed restaurant capex beneficiary through commercial kitchen equipment, labor productivity, throughput, and remodel/new-store cycles, but needs evidence of approved-vendor relationships and restaurant-chain-specific backlog.

FARM should remain a speculative shadow candidate only; its potential restaurant exposure through DSD coffee, beverage supplies, and equipment service requires verification of current customer relationships, liquidity, debt maturity, and channel profitability.

THS should remain lower priority until evidence shows material foodservice or restaurant-franchise exposure; otherwise it may be mostly a private-label grocery manufacturer with incidental restaurant relevance.
Need filings-backed market cap, leverage, valuation, analyst coverage, revenue growth, margin trends, and short-interest checks for PAR, WEST, FARM, MIDD, and THS before Layer 2C or Layer 3 scoring.
Need direct evidence of approved-vendor status, customer concentration, contract duration, and restaurant-channel revenue mix for PAR, WEST, FARM, MIDD, and THS.

Foodservice distribution consolidation appears relevant to the restaurant theme, but this candidate chunk lacks direct public-market mappings to regional distributors, GPOs, sanitation, maintenance, packaging, cold-chain logistics, and facilities-service vendors.

External evidence on WING, BRCB, and REBN suggests additional candidate nodes around franchise unit economics, loyalty-heavy coffee demand, beverage inputs, and logistics buildouts, but those tickers are outside the current chunk and should be handled in a separate candidate batch.
